Bismarck’s 1884 speech addresses workers’ insecurity and argues for state social welfare.  
This speech was part of his push for social insurance laws in Germany — the world’s first state-run health, accident, and old-age insurance programs in the 1880s.  
These reforms set a precedent that influenced other European countries to adopt similar social welfare programs over the following decades.  

Option (A) fits because Bismarck’s initiatives inspired the spread of social insurance across Europe.  
(B) is wrong because Germany was unified by then.  
(C) is wrong because communist overhaul happened much later and not due to Bismarck.  
(D) is wrong because his reforms did not cause a decrease in economic output; in fact, they aimed to stabilize the workforce.  

Final answer: (A)
